sb_prompt: WHAT SHORT AND LONG-TERM STEPS DO YOU AND THE OTHER CALLER THINK SHOULD BE TAKEN TO IMPROVE THE US BUDGET?
turns: Yeah, I get called about that a lot because I work in the library and people think I should know everything, but honestly I'm pretty skeptical about how the whole federal budget thing actually helps people like us.
Yeah, I get that, I work in carpentry and people think I'm an expert too, but honestly the budget stuff feels pretty disconnected from what's actually on the ground.
I mean, last year they cut the funding for the new teen literacy program here, so now the kids who really need help reading are just stuck with the same old books we had five years ago.

That's rough. And honestly, that's the main reason I'm so interested in this. Last month I was helping a family out in a housing project and the contractor basically told us the grant for energy-efficient windows got defunded so they had to use the old, leaky glass again. It feels like every time we fix one hole, they just cut the budget for the next repair.

Yeah, it's like we're just patching holes forever. Like, last month I tried to get funding for some used textbooks for the kids, but the pile was already gone from the cut. So I ended up just printing out old reader's guides from the archives. It works okay, but it's a band-aid, not a real fix. What about you? Have you seen any actual money go toward fixing those leaky windows, or are you in the same boat?

Yeah, that sounds terrible. Honestly, it feels like we're just throwing good money after bad. I mean, we put in the bid for those windows last spring, hoping the surplus from the road resurfacing would cover it, but then the city just said nope, no funds. So yeah, we're stuck in the same boat, patching holes until the next freeze hits.
Yeah, I guess we're just waiting for the next freeze to happen, isn't that it?

Yeah, I guess so. I mean, it's just frustrating because I've got three kids at home and the heating bill is already double what it used to be. It feels like the whole system is just... waiting for the next crisis to see if they'll pull out their pocketbook again.

Yeah, it's just exhausting knowing that my own kids are gonna be stuck reading those same recycled guides next semester, and I wonder if there's even a long-term plan that doesn't involve just hoping the government figures out how to fix it before we run out of options entirely.
I guess the long-term thing is, maybe we need to stop letting these projects die because someone's holding onto the surplus instead of actually spending it on things that keep people warm.

Yeah, but honestly, the long-term part is just really hard to pin down, maybe we just need to force them to actually vote on fixing the core stuff instead of keeping that surplus money just sitting there?
Yeah, that's exactly it. Maybe we need to stop letting the money sit in that surplus account and just spend it on the actual stuff before the next crisis hits.
Yeah, that would be great, but honestly, the way I see it, they'd have to stop treating the surplus like a safety net and actually use it to build the foundation first instead of just band-aid fixes.

Yeah, but the thing is, if we just dump the surplus without a plan, they might blow it all on something that's not even needed, so maybe we need a rule where that money actually has to go toward the foundation stuff first before they can touch it?
Yeah, that sounds like a rule we could actually make, but I'm not sure if they'd even let it pass if it meant the surplus disappears completely.
Right, but I guess that rule would be hard to sell if they say we don't have the "safety net" for the next winter yet.
Yeah, maybe that's the problem, if they don't admit the safety net is actually a trap waiting to happen.
Right, but I mean, if we made that rule, they'd probably just shift all the other maintenance funds into that same surplus account, so yeah, I don't know if that actually gets it done.

That's the thing, though, if you just lock the money down like that, the people running the show might just find a different excuse to delay it, or they'll shift it somewhere else entirely and we're back to square one before the next freeze even hits.
Yeah, I mean, maybe we'd have to attach something to the bill that says if they don't spend the surplus on the core stuff first, they just can't touch any other budget lines until they do.
Yeah, but honestly, if you tie their hands that tight, they'll just find some other weird loophole to delay the whole thing until it's too late again.

Yeah, but honestly, if they really want to stop the loopholes, maybe we need to just make the funding automatic so nobody can vote it out before it gets used, rather than trying to force them to admit the safety net is broken.
Yeah, but if you make it automatic like that, they might just find a way to sink it into the general fund first so it never actually reaches the families until the bill is already dead.
Yeah, but if you make it automatic, they just sink it into the general fund first so it never actually reaches the families until the bill is already dead.
Yeah, that's the nightmare scenario, it's like they just hide it in the big pile and nobody ever asks about it again.
Yeah, but maybe the rule needs to say that once they move it to the general fund, the whole thing gets cancelled for a year so they have to ask for it again?
I don't know, maybe that's too extreme, like setting off a fire alarm just to get someone to leave the room, but I suppose it'd force them to actually show up at the table.
Yeah, I guess that's the risk, it's like you're screaming at them to pay attention but they just turn up the volume on the general fund and nobody hears you.
Yeah, but maybe instead of cancelling the whole thing, we could just make the deadline non-negotiable so they don't have to wait for a vote to get it done?
Yeah, but maybe the deadline needs to be like, six months from the bill signing, so they can't just drag their feet until the winter starts anyway.

Yeah, six months sounds about right, because honestly if I have to wait another year to find these kids a book that's not falling apart, I don't think they'll even be in school when the deadline hits.
Yeah, six months is probably enough time before the kids start falling behind, so let's push for that.
Yeah, if we make that hard deadline, it might actually force them to just do it before they can hide it forever.
Yeah, let's push for that, because honestly I'd rather we have a working draft than a fancy promise that goes nowhere.

Yeah, let's make that hard deadline, because honestly if I have to wait another year to find these kids a book that's not falling apart, I don't think they'll even be in school when the deadline hits.
Yeah, I agree, if we set a hard deadline like that, maybe they'd stop hiding behind excuses and actually get the windows installed before the pipes burst.
Yeah, six months, that actually feels like the only way to stop them from just talking circles forever.
Yeah, that's probably the only way to make it stick.
Yeah, if we don't do that before the pipes actually burst, we're just wasting the money on empty promises again.
Yeah, but honestly if we wait until the pipes actually burst, we're just throwing good money after bad again.
